blurb: Storing heavy things low, stacking stably, keeping routes and fire exits clear, and reporting damaged shelving.

cards.title: Safe Stacking & Storage
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- store items at the right height
- keep walkways and fire exits clear
- report damaged or overloaded shelving

cards.title: Tidy stores are safer
cards.body: Poor storage causes a surprising number of injuries, from items falling on people to blocked walkways and toppling stacks. A tidy, well-organised store is nicer to work in, genuinely safer, and saves time.

cards.title: Heavy low, light high
cards.body: Store heavier items at around waist height, where they are easy to lift without bending low or reaching high, and keep lighter items up top. Do not stack too high or lean stacks against each other. Take from the top of a stack, and use proper steps for high shelves rather than climbing.

items.title: Stock
items.text: Off the floor, on shelving or racking.

cards.title: Never block the way out
cards.body: Stock should be off the floor and never left blocking walkways, doorways or, most importantly, fire exits, even briefly. A box left in a corridor is a trip hazard and could block an escape route in an emergency.

left.title: Do
items: Keep stock on shelving or racking
Use proper steps for high shelves

cards.title: Look after it
cards.body: Do not overload shelves beyond what they are rated for. Report any that are damaged, wobbly or overloaded so they can be fixed before they fail.

items.title: Report it
items.text: So it is fixed before it fails.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Heavy low, light high, stacks stable, routes clear
- Never block walkways, doorways or fire exits, even briefly
- Keep stock off the floor
- Use proper steps, never climb racking
- Report damaged, wobbly or overloaded shelves

cards.q: Heavier items should be stored at…
cards.why: Waist height means heavier items are easy to lift without bending low or reaching high.

cards.q: Stacking things too high or leaning stacks together is unsafe.
cards.why: That is how a whole shelf comes down on someone.

cards.q: Where should stock NEVER be stored, even briefly?
options: Blocking walkways, doorways or fire exits
On shelving at waist height, well within its rating
On racking, off the floor and stable
In the cellar on a pallet against the wall
cards.why: A box left in a corridor is a trip hazard and could block an escape route in an emergency.

cards.q: Stock should be kept off the floor on shelving or racking.
cards.why: It keeps routes clear and stock stable.

cards.q: To reach a high shelf you should…
options: Stretch and lean on the shelf
cards.why: Use proper steps rather than climbing.

cards.q: You should overload shelves to fit everything in.
cards.why: Do not load shelves beyond what they are rated for.

cards.q: What should you do about a wobbly or damaged shelf?
options: Stack lighter items on it only
Take your own stock off it and say nothing
Prop it up and carry on
Report it so it can be fixed before it fails
cards.why: Report any damaged, wobbly or overloaded shelving so it can be fixed before it fails.

options: At the front of a walkway
cards.why: Keep lighter items up top and heavier items at waist height.

cards.q: A box left in a corridor could block an escape route in an emergency.
cards.why: It is also a trip hazard.

cards.q: Complete the rule: heavy low, light high, stacks stable, routes…
cards.why: Heavy low, light high, stacks stable, routes clear keeps your store a safe place to work.
